findings.title: A time-curve pullback does not supply a single-valued observed solution on that curve
findings.evidence: G1.4 supplies only a holomorphic time map C→B and an admissible observer, then promises meromorphic evaluation on that curve. N1.7 requires an actual holomorphic phase map s:C→M. The constructed complete flat connection supplies a section on the pointed universal cover of C; descent to C is a separate condition.
findings.falsification: The roadmap’s own sign-monodromy connection q′=q/(2t) over C=ℂ× with observation Q=q and nonzero initial value has a well-defined non-infinite observation on the universal cover, but no single-valued meromorphic evaluation on C.
findings.required_change: State the conditional theorem with a chosen initial point and evaluation on the pointed universal cover C̃. Evaluation descends to C precisely under scalar monodromy/deck invariance. Alternatively require an actual horizontal section on C as input. Retain this as an in-scope theorem under additional hypotheses; update EN, JA, plan and appendix.

findings.title: The analytic-space to native-manifold comparison needs topological hypotheses
findings.evidence: The constructed analytic category is specified only by local coherent ideal quotients of polydiscs, but every smooth object is then identified with the native complex-manifold carrier. Those local axioms do not imply Hausdorffness or second countability.
findings.falsification: The complex line with doubled origin is a smooth locally polydisc analytic space but is not Hausdorff. An uncountable disjoint union of complex lines is smooth and Hausdorff but not second countable. Neither is in the declared native manifold scope.
findings.required_change: Require Hausdorffness and second countability (or the exact equivalent native hypotheses) for the smooth-object/manifold comparison, and prove them for the separated finite-type analytifications and admitted smooth-base pullbacks used by this roadmap. Keep broader analytic gluing only with its own stated category and restrictions.

findings.title: Picard smoothness must use affine square-zero tests or relative cohomological dimension
findings.evidence: The new bullet quantifies over a square-zero thickening T₀↪T, places the obstruction in absolute H²(C_T₀,p*I), and calls for the cohomological-dimension vanishing on proper relative curves. Relative dimension one alone does not make this absolute group vanish for nonaffine T₀.
findings.falsification: Take T₀=ℙ²_ℂ, C_T₀=ℙ¹×T₀ and I=O_ℙ²(−3), with the split square-zero thickening defined by O_T₀⊕I. Then H²(C_T₀,p*I)≅ℂ. The relative Picard functor can nevertheless be smooth.
findings.required_change: Prove R²p_*(p*I)=0 and the absolute vanishing on affine square-zero test bases, or use the exact affine argument in Stacks tag0DPJ/0DPK. For arbitrary test bases formulate local lifting and descent/sheafification, not global vanishing of this H² group. The obstruction and torsor statements themselves remain valid.

findings.title: Polarization independence contains an unresolved backward reference to the moduli universal property
findings.evidence: M1.2 now constructs a polarization and compares its choices by the moduli universal property. The stable-connection moduli universal property is constructed in M2.1, which already depends on M1.2. The machine graph is acyclic only because this prose edge is unrecorded.
findings.required_change: Keep positivity, relative ampleness and local very ampleness in M1.2. Compare auxiliary embeddings through common tensor powers/presentations there, or move independence of the resulting stable-moduli construction to M2.1 after its universal property is proved. If an existing Quot universal property was intended, name it explicitly and supply its exact dependency rather than referring to the later moduli theorem.

findings.title: The zero-form falsification case excludes zero-dimensional fibers
findings.evidence: The diagnostic says the relative zero form is vertically degenerate without a positive-dimension qualification. On a zero-dimensional vertical tangent space, the zero alternating form is nondegenerate. The framework admits this case, including rank-one fixed-determinant fibers.
findings.required_change: Say that the relative zero form is degenerate on a positive-dimensional fiber. Preserve the theorem’s valid zero-dimensional case.

findings.title: Japanese 2-categorical coherence is mistranslated as two-stage coherence
findings.evidence: English “2-coherent descent” and “base-change/2-coherence” appear as “2段階の整合的降下” and “2段階の整合性”. The 2 refers to coherence of 2-isomorphisms, not a construction performed in two stages.
